                [32m'## Background\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Build a Godot 4 high-level multiplayer lobby that runs an ENet host **and** several ENet clients inside a single headless Godot process using loopback (`127.0.0.1`). The host spawns a `Player` node for each connecting peer through a `MultiplayerSpawner`. Each `Player` carries a `MultiplayerSynchronizer` that replicates state, plus an RPC that lets any peer mutate the per-player score and have the change propagated to every other peer.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Requirements\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Core Requirements\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Implement the project so a single invocation of `godot --headless` is enough to start the server, spin up N ENet clients on the same machine, exchange `MultiplayerSynchronizer` state, dispatch a score-update RPC from every client, and write a final-state JSON.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Players are spawned dynamically through `MultiplayerSpawner` (no hard-coded children in `Players` in the scene file).\n'[39m +
                [32m"* Each `Player` node's *multiplayer authority* equals the peer ID it represents (the host's player has authority `1`, client players have authority equal to their unique multiplayer ID).\n"[39m +
                [32m'* A `MultiplayerSynchronizer` on each `Player` replicates the `Player.position` (Vector2) to every peer.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* A `@rpc("any_peer", "call_local")` function with exact signature `update_score(value: int)` mutates an integer `score` field on the `Player`.\n'[39m +

                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Project Structure and Required Files\n'[39m +

                [32m'The project must be located at `/home/user/myproject` and contain the following files:\n'[39m +

                [32m'* `/home/user/myproject/main.gd`\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `/home/user/myproject/player.tscn` (root node named `Player`, script `res://player.gd`, contains a child `MultiplayerSynchronizer` that replicates `Player:position`)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `/home/user/myproject/player.gd`\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +

                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'```gdscript\n'[39m +
                [32m'@rpc("any_peer", "call_local")\n'[39m +
                [32m'func update_score(value: int) -> void:\n'[39m +
                [32m'    score += value\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Execution and CLI Arguments\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The project will be executed using the following command:\n'[39m +
                [32m'`godot --headless --path /home/user/myproject res://main.tscn -- --port=<port> --clients=<n> --frames=<frames> --score-deltas=<csv> --out=<json_path>`\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Your script must parse these custom arguments passed after the `--` separator:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `--port`: The port to run the server on and connect clients to.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `--clients`: The number of client peers to spawn.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `--frames`: The number of frames to pump before writing the state and exiting.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `--score-deltas`: A comma-separated list of integers representing the score deltas to apply to clients.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `--out`: The output path where the final-state JSON must be written.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The process must exit with status `0` after writing the JSON.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Output JSON Schema and Semantics\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'After successful execution, the file at `<json_path>` must exist and conform to the following schema:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                [32m'{\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "server": {\n'[39m +
                [32m'    "unique_id": 1,\n'[39m +
                [32m'    "peers": [<int>, ...],\n'[39m +
                [32m'    "players": {\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "<peer_id>": {"authority": <peer_id>, "position": [<x>, <y>], "score": <int>}\n'[39m +
                [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "clients": [\n'[39m +
                [32m'    {\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "unique_id": <int>,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "peers": [<int>, ...],\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "players": {\n'[39m +
                [32m'        "<peer_id>": {"authority": <peer_id>, "position": [<x>, <y>], "score": <int>}\n'[39m +
                [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ]\n'[39m +
                [32m'}\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'#### JSON Semantics:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Peer-id keys inside `"players"` must be JSON strings, and the list of `"peers"` must be sorted in ascending order.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `server.unique_id` must be `1`.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* `server.peers` must equal the sorted list of every client's `unique_id` (the host/server does not list itself).\n"[39m +
                [32m"* Every client's `peers` list must equal the sorted list of all other peer IDs, including the server (`1`).\n"[39m +
                [32m"* `players` keys must be identical across all peers and equal to the set of every connected peer's `unique_id` (one `Player` per peer in the lobby, including the host).\n"[39m +
                [32m"* Each player's `authority` must equal its key.\n"[39m +
                [32m"* Each player's `position` must equal `[authority, authority]` (set by the authoritative peer; values are 32-bit floats and small precision loss is allowed for large peer IDs). For example, the host (authority `1`) must set its position to `Vector2(1, 1)`, and client with ID `12345` must set its position to `Vector2(12345, 12345)`.\n"[39m +
                [32m"* Each player's `score` must equal the score delta passed for the matching client index (the host's player score stays `0` because the host does not call the RPC).\n"[39m +
                [32m'* The `clients` array must preserve the CLI client order: index 0 corresponds to the first client spawned, etc.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Implementation Hints\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Use `ENetMultiplayerPeer.create_server(port, max_clients)` for the host and `ENetMultiplayerPeer.create_client("127.0.0.1", port)` for each client.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* Run all peers in **one** Godot process by giving each peer its own `SceneMultiplayer` instance and attaching it to a distinct subtree via `SceneTree.set_multiplayer(api, NodePath)`. RPC paths are resolved relative to each multiplayer root, so put the spawner/players at the same *relative* path under every peer's root.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* The `MultiplayerSpawner` should reference `res://player.tscn` in its `_spawnable_scenes` and point its `spawn_path` at the `Players` container.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* Set the player's authority via `set_multiplayer_authority(peer_id)` on the server right after the host spawns it; the synchronizer will propagate the position written by the authority.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* Pump frames by repeatedly calling `await get_tree().process_frame` from a coroutine. Quit with `get_tree().quit()` once the final-state JSON has been written.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* The CLI flag `--score-deltas` provides a comma-separated list of integers; the i-th client must invoke `update_score.rpc(deltas[i])` exactly once on its own player after the spawn is observed.'[39m

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +

Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When users ask you to perform tasks, check if any of the available skills below can help complete the task more effectively. Skills provide specialized capabilities and domain knowledge.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When users ask about a SPECIFIC skill (e.g., "How does the pdf skill work?", "What does the commit skill do?"), you must call this tool to get detailed information about that skill.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m"This tool returns the skill's detailed instructions which you must then follow to complete the task. The instructions contain step-by-step guidance on how to perform the specific task or workflow.\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'How to invoke:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Use this tool with the skill name\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Example: `skill: "pdf-processing"` - invoke the pdf-processing skill\n'[39m +
            [32m"- The tool will return the skill's instructions\n"[39m +
            [32m'- Follow the returned instructions carefully to complete the task\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When a skill is relevant for a task OR when users ask about a SPECIFIC skill, you must invoke this tool IMMEDIATELY as your first action\n'[39m +
            [32m'- For general questions about available skills, simply refer to the "Available skills" list below without calling this tool\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER just announce or mention a skill in your text response without actually calling this tool (except for general skill listing requests)\n'[39m +
            [32m'- This is a BLOCKING REQUIREMENT: invoke the relevant Skill tool BEFORE generating any other response about a specific skill or task\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Only use skills listed in "Available skills" below\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Check compatibility requirements before using a skill - ensure the skill is compatible with the current OS/environment\n'[39m +
            [32m'- After calling this tool, follow the returned instructions step by step\n'[39m +
            [32m'- The skill file location is shown in the [Location: filepath] section of each skill listing below - use this information to understand where the skill is defined\n'[39m +
            [32m"- Use the directory containing the skill's source file as the base directory for resolving any resource files mentioned in the instructions\n"[39m +

            [32m'It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'## When to Use This Tool\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'## Task States and Management\n'[39m +
